question: Does the newly elected sixteen-fit blend also help on both previously registered, independently reshuffled connected-group fold allocations? A one-row designated gain prompted this post-hoc transfer check. Freeze the recipe from the autonomous seal before measuring any individual sixteen-fit combination on these partitions.
source: Read the actual single or vote contents and score mode from the locked 16-fit raw control. Use only those existing row-aligned, class-aligned frozen per-model probabilities. The two explicit comparisons are the default ten-fit model and the earlier expanded-budget dual-encoder model, each taken from its own recorded autonomous election. No new method, weight or selection.
analysis: Report each of ten matched held-fold accuracies and gained/lost counts. Sum each five-fold partition separately: both cover the same 8301 training rows. Do not pool them as independent observations. A positive stability signal for the sixteen-fit choice versus the usual default requires at least +0.30 percentage points on each allocation and strictly positive gains on at least seven of the ten folds. Report performance against the alternative dual encoder without a second promotion decision.
usage: This study reads historical training-fitted models and predictions only. Zero new fits, zero API, no designated validation labels, formal test, or H2.
